subject: HaloAI committed capacity — latency profile, tokens/sec estimates, and buffer sizing

Subject: HaloAI committed capacity — initial numbers and timelines

Hi Neha / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week. The execs are inclined to move forward with a reserved capacity commitment — target start date July 15. They asked for a short note from Redwood that maps the committed token run-rate to an expected latency profile and the recommended safety buffer (GPU slab sizing) so procurement can finalize the contract.

Quick specifics from our side:
- Estimated steady-state peak: 1.8M tokens/day (mixed chat + few multiline generation workloads).
- Expected burst window: ~6x steady-state for 10–15 minutes, 3x for 1 hour.
- P95 latency target for session completions: <= 450ms (user-facing short chat flows); P99 target: <= 900ms.

Can you share a short mapping (tokens/sec, slab sizing, expected p95/p99 with and without KV cache warm cache, and recommended headroom for the first 90 days)? Procurement wants the note attached to the MSA.

Appreciate it — Olivia
HaloAI (Olivia Chen)

Olivia — thanks, this is helpful. Attaching a short one-pager (haloai_commit_summary.xlsx) and looping in Priyom and Karthik for the detailed slab math. High level:

- We’ll translate 1.8M tokens/day into tokens/sec using your traffic profile. If peak concurrency maps to ~90k tokens/minute (~1.5k tokens/sec) sustained during burst windows, that suggests a mid-sized dedicated slab with headroom.
- KV cache warm dramatically improves tail latencies for chat-style flows; we’ll show p95/p99 both cold and warm.
- Proposal will include a canary plan (10% of traffic on day 1), automatic fallback to a slightly higher-latency but cheaper model if your slab is saturated, and a 25% initial safety buffer for month 1–3 while patterns stabilize.

Requested from you: a sample hour-of-day distribution (even coarse) and whether the burst is typically synchronized from customers or isolated to a few sessions. That changes slab vs. auto-burst sizing.

Ben / Priyom / Karthik — can you weigh in on model variant sizing and a proposed tokens/sec -> GPU-slab mapping? I sketched a few numbers in the attachment but want the math in thread so procurement can see assumptions.

Thanks — Neha

Neha / team — added the numeric breakdown below and attached a quick CSV (proposed-slab-sizing.csv) with per-model tokens/sec capacity and slab counts. Summary math and assumptions are called out at top.

Assumptions (short):
- Workload mix: 70% chat-style (context windows avg 1.5k tokens/session), 30% multi-turn long generation (avg 6k tokens/session).
- Average tokens per request: ~900 tokens.
- Peak sustained tokens/sec during burst (6x steady for 15 min) = steady tokens/sec * 6.
- Default model: resizable open model (quantized) with baseline single-GPU throughput ~18k tokens/sec for short-chat optimized path; long-gen reduces effective throughput to ~9k tokens/sec (memory/KV pressure).

Math (high level):
- Steady-state: 1.8M tokens/day -> 20.83 tokens/sec (1,800,000 / 86400).
- But traffic is spiky; translate to expected TPS at peak concurrency. We estimate peak concurrent-request multiplier (from traffic shape supplied by HaloAI) of ~70x steady for short bursts -> 1,458 tokens/sec peak.
- Required GPU capacity (short-chat optimized): 1,458 / 18,000 = 0.081 GPUs effective. With batching inefficiencies and scheduling overhead, use effective utilization cap 60% -> need 0.135 GPUs.
- For long-gen mix this increases: worst-case mixed demand during bursts -> equivalent of 0.27 GPUs.

Slab sizing recommendation (initial commit):
- Minimum dedicated slab: 1 x small slab (4 x A100-sim equiv GPUs) to meet burst headroom and support redundancy. Rationale: single-GPU math is useful but production SLOs + system overhead and model warm caches need multi-GPU slab to handle KV distribution and autoscaling cushion.
- Safety buffer: recommend 30% for month 0–3 given unknown traffic shape and cache warm-up. That maps to keeping 1 additional GPU worth of spare capacity for failover.
- Burst policy: allow temporary autoscale to a 2-slab burst pool (8 GPUs) for short peaks tied to commit windows; chargeable in burst clause.

Expected latencies (approx):
- Cold start (cache cold): p95 ~700–900ms, p99 ~1.6s (long-gen paths push this).
- Warm cache steady: p95 ~320–420ms, p99 ~600–900ms depending on mix and batching.

Operational recommendations:
- Canary: route 10% traffic for 48–72 hours, verify KV hit rates and tail latencies before full cutover.
- Telemetry: enable token-level latency breakdowns and per-route p95/p99 dashboards; create an alert for p99 > 1s.
- Rollouts: we can do a phased increase in commit visibility tied to billed tokens (month 1: 60% traffic; month 2: 85%; month 3: 100%).

I attached proposed-slab-sizing.csv with: model variant throughput rows, tokens/sec per GPU, effective concurrent sessions, and suggested slab counts for steady, burst, and buffer. Happy to refine if Olivia can share a simple hourly distribution.

— Priyom
Senior Infra SRE, Redwood Inference

- We agree to the 25–30% safety buffer for the first 90 days. Procurement will include an autoscale burst clause tied to additional token usage.
